title: Daylight saving time ends Nov. 1, 2026: is the change still on?
dek: Clocks fall back at 2 a.m. on Sunday, November 1. The House passed the Sunshine Protection Act in July, but it has not become law.
keywords: when does daylight saving time end 2026
keyPoints: Daylight saving time ends Sunday, November 1, 2026, at 2 a.m. local time.
Clocks go back one hour, so sunset comes about an hour earlier in the evening.
The House passed the Sunshine Protection Act on July 14, 2026; as of September it had not passed the Senate.
Hawaii and most of Arizona do not change their clocks.

sources.title: Daylight Saving Time 2026: When do clocks fall back?

body: With October here, a lot of people are asking whether we still change the clocks this year. The answer is yes. Daylight saving time ends on Sunday, November 1, 2026. At 2 a.m., clocks fall back one hour to 1 a.m., which gives most people an extra hour of sleep that night.

There has been talk of ending the switch. The U.S. House passed the Sunshine Protection Act on July 14, 2026, which would make daylight saving time permanent all year. According to AccuWeather, as of September the bill had not passed the Senate or become law, so the usual schedule stays in place for now.

Once the clocks change, sunset will come about an hour earlier in the evening, and mornings will be lighter. Hawaii and most of Arizona do not observe daylight saving time, so their clocks stay put, although the Navajo Nation in Arizona does make the change.
Most phones and computers update on their own. Car clocks, microwaves, ovens and some wall clocks usually do not, and those are the ones that cause confusion on Monday morning.
With a month to go, you can plan one small thing now, such as moving an evening walk or a child's outdoor play time a little earlier in November so it still happens in daylight.
